structure.notes: The report reads as a lab notebook appended over three days: results for one topic sit in three or four places (predation in sections 'Predation', 'Solitary hunters', 'LONE', 'RELS', 'Relations for arrivals'; groups at once in 'Groups', the third-round table, the sweep). Merge by topic, putting first-day single-run results and their overnight replications in the same table with an n column so the reader sees what replicated (MEANDERER, PRONE_TO_RAGE, cohesion) and what didn't (FLEEQUICK, VISION_ARC, VIEWRANGE, cave toad, crawler). Move every 'your note / your ruling / your call' Q&A into the design-history appendix and write the body in the third person ('the user ruled on 30 Sep'). Keep one status for v7.0 and one recommendations table. The summary should lead with the relation rule and its placement caveat, then the five or six results that drive the tool (BENIGN switch, reach, group size, leader cohesion, FREQUENCY proportional, ladder x0.5), each with n.

prose.before: Over 300 cells and 10 spawn-time runs, with one or two replicates, tested it and the questions below on the rig on 29–30 Sep 2026.
prose.after: The rig tested this rule and the questions below in about N cells and M spawn-time runs between 29 Sep and 1 Oct 2026, mostly with one or two replicates.

prose.before: The one refinement: DF itself relates every unit that isn't flagged wild (dwarves, livestock, placed animals, and groups the tool releases) to each new wild arrival, so placed hunters attacked native wildlife the test never related them to (RELS).
prose.after: One caveat: DF treats any animal a script places, or the tool releases, as a fort animal. It then writes a predator relation from it toward each new wild arrival, which is why placed hunters attacked native wildlife (RELS).

prose.before: One fixed value moves the map: the predator ladder.
prose.after: Of the tool's fixed values, only the predator FREQUENCY ladder changed how many predators the map holds.

prose.before: v6.9 (released 30 Sep) fixed the ecology write: it now checks reach, arms any non-BENIGN carnivore. Builder v2.2 has been run offline, and tool v7.0 is built on a branch but not yet deployed; in v7.0 the tool's own season deal overrides NO_<season>.
prose.after: v6.9 (released 30 Sep) checks reach before writing a relation and arms any non-BENIGN carnivore. v7.0 adds the roster builder and lets the tool's season deal override NO_<season>; it passes the full validator (214 PASS, 0 FAIL) but is not yet merged or pushed.

prose.before: DF hunts only on a predator relation, written by the tool or, over longer runs, by DF itself (RELP), and any attacker that is not BENIGN carries it out.
prose.after: An animal hunts only when it holds a predator relation toward its prey and is not BENIGN. On the surface, only the tool writes such relations between wild animals.

prose.before: Up to v6.8 the tool's ecology write got this wrong both ways.
prose.after: Up to v6.8 the tool left amphibious predators out of the ecology and wrote ocean predators against land prey.

prose.before: The surface rules hold on every water body. Underground, some species fight with no relation written and others do not, so the tool keeps writing cavern relations.
prose.after: Rivers, lakes, oceans and cavern pools follow the surface rules. In the caverns some species fight with no relation written, so the tool still writes cavern relations for the rest.

prose.before: Of the ~95 tokens asked about, three flags and one value change wildlife behaviour measurably within 3,000 ticks: BENIGN, CRAZED, OPPOSED_TO_LIFE, and PRONE_TO_RAGE at 25 or more.
prose.after: Within 3,000 ticks, five tokens changed behaviour in a way that replicated or was unmistakable: BENIGN, CRAZED, OPPOSED_TO_LIFE, MEANDERER and PRONE_TO_RAGE at 25 or more.

prose.before: 16 of the tokens asked about appear in no creature definition, not 9, and 6 of those still exist in play.
prose.after: Sixteen of the tokens appear in no creature definition; six of them still occur in play, added by world generation or by syndromes.

prose.before: Raw NO_<season> flag or the tool: which wins depends on who brings the animal. DF's own pick honours the flag even when it is set at run time: NO_SPRING stopped 19 of 19 spring kangaroo waves (T2).
prose.after: DF's pick honours NO_<season> even when it is set at run time: a FREQUENCY-100 kangaroo with NO_SPRING took 0 of 19 spring waves (T2). v7.0 therefore clears the flag on the species it manages, so its own season deal wins.

prose.before: 'As residents' means animals meant to stay on the map for their season, whether the tool placed them or DF drew them.
prose.after: A resident is an animal meant to stay on the map for its season, whether the tool placed it or DF drew it.

prose.before: On land and in the caverns, DF draws every group; the tool only opens or closes the gate (the limit, stock, FREQUENCY, seasons). The tool draws water groups itself (Driver B), and places animals only on a command (`place`).
prose.after: DF draws every land and cavern group; the tool only controls whether they come (limit, stock, FREQUENCY, seasons). The tool draws water groups itself and places animals only when told to.

prose.before: Activity time only shatters the guilds into one-species cells and has no documented fortress effect.
prose.after: Activity time (diurnal, nocturnal) splits the guilds into single-species groups and has no documented effect in fortress mode, so it is left out.

prose.before: The rules are sound in intent. As written, they never finish filling their slots, and they demote the classic pack hunters to vermin-eaters.
prose.after: The rules are sound in intent, but as written they never fill their slots, and their size bands class wolves, hyenas and cougars as small predators that may eat only vermin.

prose.before: Over 54,560 builds (11 embark types × every layer × 4 seasons × 20 seeds × 11 configurations), no roster had an isolated or split animal (v2.0; v2.1 split cavern rosters, v2.2 restored 0%), mutual predation, or a humanoid-rule break.
prose.after: In 54,560 builds, no v2.0 or v2.2 roster had an isolated animal, mutual predation or a broken humanoid rule. v2.1 split every cavern roster, which v2.2 fixed.

prose.before: The gate let a group of n hunters take prey up to 5 × one hunter's mass × n^0.75, so the pack needed grows as (prey/predator ÷ 5)^4/3.
prose.after: The gate allowed a pack of n hunters to take prey up to 5 × n^0.75 times one hunter's mass. Prey 25 times a wolf's mass therefore needed a pack of about 9.

prose.before: DF's combat turns on pack size, not prey size.
prose.after: In DF's combat, the number of hunters mattered more than the size of the prey.

prose.before: At the first proposal (apex 1 against prey 8) an apex group would arrive about once in four seasons, too rare to see predation at all. Kill rates are low enough that prey can afford a larger predator share: even a 10-hyena clan takes about 13 prey a season, against 30–40 prey arriving.
prose.after: At apex 1 against prey 8, an apex group would arrive about once in four seasons, too rarely to see. Kill rates leave room for more predators: a 10-hyena clan takes about 13 prey a season, while 30–40 arrive.

prose.before: Whatever the skill does, it works in the fight.
prose.after: So the Sneak skill, if it helps at all, helps in combat, not by hiding the hunter.

prose.before: P1's rule still holds as stated: hunting needs a PREDATOR_OR_PREY entry. But DF adds such entries on its own over time, and the tool's writes come on top of them. How fast and between whom is a new tracker item.
prose.after: Hunting still needs a PREDATOR_OR_PREY entry, but DF wrote one here for the placed hunter on its own. RELS later showed why: DF treats placed animals as fort animals.

prose.before: Every pelagic species now has a predator, and every BENIGN attacker the roster arms is cleared, so DF can act on every unit edge except the 19% whose reach is untested.
prose.after: Every pelagic species now has a predator and every armed predator has BENIGN cleared. DF can act on 81% of unit edges; the other 19% have untested reach.

prose.before: Builder v2.2 (offline) and tool v7.0 (committed on a local branch, not deployed) take your design principle: where the tool manages an ecological space, it overrides vanilla DF instead of running alongside it.
prose.after: Builder v2.2 and tool v7.0 follow the user's principle: where the tool manages part of the ecology, it overrides DF rather than running alongside it.

prose.before: Flying stays at 19% because a flying roster holds an apex and 1–2 raptors against at most 4 bird species; going lower needs a smaller raptor slot, not FREQUENCY.
prose.after: Flying stays at 19% predators because a flying roster has one apex and one or two raptors against at most four bird species. Only a smaller raptor slot, not FREQUENCY, would lower it.

prose.before: LONE10 (10 runs per arm, 30 Sep night) settles it: the package lifts kills.
prose.after: With 10 runs per arm (LONE10), the package cougar killed more: 49 animals against 21 (p = 0.024), 29 against 14 of them placed prey (p = 0.07).

prose.before: Its filter still sees released groups, because DFHack's wildlife test reads the population reference, not the wild flag. Its refought counter will show how often DF writes them back.
prose.after: The sweep still recognises released groups as wildlife, because DFHack's wildlife test reads the population reference rather than the wild flag. A counter records how often DF writes a cleared pair back.

prose.before: The overnight blocks closed every open item in the tracker except the final validation. Five of them needed a rerun after the first pass tested nothing or was confounded: SW3, SCV2 and S8C tested nothing, and SW1 and SW2 were confounded by cell order.
prose.after: The overnight and morning blocks closed every tracker item. Six needed a rerun: INV, SW3, SCV2 and S8C tested nothing, and SW1 and SW2 were confounded by cell order.

prose.before: DF's own behaviour and the rig's walk-and-eat verbs cleared them only for wolves on land. What the night didn't measure is which species did the eating.
prose.after: DF removed no carcasses on its own, and the rig's walk-and-eat verbs worked only for wolves on land. Which species ate in the tool's pass was not recorded.

prose.before: Each row reads "the writer's row holds this toward the target".
prose.after: Each row gives the relation the writer holds toward the target in DF's relation table.

prose.before: What the night taught the method. The first sweep cells shared one fort load per replicate and always ran in the same order.
prose.after: The first sweep runs had a design flaw: the cells of a replicate shared one fort load and always ran in the same order.

prose.before: Every item below is done; v7.0 validates at 214 PASS, 0 FAIL. What remains are your decisions on what the night found. None of them is applied to the tool yet:
prose.after: All tracker items are done (Appendix D). These decisions remain, none yet applied to the tool:

prose.before: Almost no vanilla swimmer counts as a scavenger. The tool counts a creature as a scavenger only if it eats bone or curious-beast food, or is on a short named list.
prose.after: The tool counts a creature as a scavenger only if it is BONECARN, a CURIOUSBEAST_EATER or on a short named list, which leaves just three vanilla swimmers: pond grabbers, sea serpents and sea monsters.

prose.before: The lion is faster than every prey here and still made 1 kill in 4 CAL cells. A solitary hunter's problem is engaging at all, not catching up.
prose.after: The lion outruns every prey here yet killed once in 4 CAL cells: a lone hunter's problem is finding prey, not catching it.

prose.before: A gap the first run found: dogs, cats, pigs and chickens have no BIOME in the raws, so the tool classed them 'unclassified' and its forgotten-beast safety filter (`fb_safe`) kept them out of every pairing.
prose.after: The first run exposed a bug: dogs, cats, pigs and chickens have no BIOME in the raws, so the tool's safety filter for forgotten beasts (`fb_safe`) excluded them from every pairing.

prose.before: Giant jackal packs carried the overshoot on BOATS: wave counts stayed modest, but each pack is large. CTRL undershoots because its supply is mostly ravens.
prose.after: On BOATS, giant jackal packs caused the overshoot: few waves, but large packs. CTRL undershot because DF sends it mostly ravens.

summary: 1. LONE10 is misreported (l.20, l.620, Rec 16, items 4/7/34). Placed-prey kills were 14 -> 29 (p = 0.07), not '9 against 7'. The quoted p = 0.025 belongs to all kills (21 -> 49), and the native share of those is a placement artefact. Restate it with both metrics and the caveat, and add LONE10 to findings.md. 2. The placed-units-are-non-wild caveat (RELS row 3) must move into Methods and be footnoted on CAL, STL/STL2, LONE/LONE10, PK, GPK and the SW1/SW2 arena. It explains the off-target kills and weakens the floor/sneak and prey-choice conclusions. Rewrite the RELP-era 'DF writes relations itself over time' lines (l.49, l.467, l.615). 3. Give v7.0 one status everywhere: on the rig, validated 214/0, not merged or pushed. Then fix the stale recommendation statuses (Rec 12 depth survey, 14 port, 15 realms, 16 p-value, 17 good/evil, 20 fishers on) and reconcile 17 vs 23 validator checks. 4. Correct the summary overstatements: sharks did attack shore seals (53 attacks, 1 kill); surface wild-wild relations are 'almost never' (5 of 370), not 'never'; 'one fixed value moves the map' ignores SW3B/SW5; 'depth cannot separate' contradicts the depth-gated pelagic rule; 'DF never draws SAVAGE' rests on one species, one fort, 2 runs. 5. Fix the NO_SPRING misstatement: the kangaroo took 0 of 19 spring waves; spring waves were not stopped. It is wrong on l.189 and in Rec 5 ('100% of spring waves'). 6. Update the stale results: vermin predation is tested (VRM2/VRM4, not 'untested'); cave toads and crawlers fight at one spot (HC4); MEANDERER replicated (so not 'three flags and one value'); VIEWRANGE did not clearly replicate (its 40-tile arm equals the control). 7. Fix the leader claims: in L2 the largest-male herd spread 41.9 tiles against 11.7 for lowest-id, so 'as well as' and 'both within 2-4 tiles' are wrong. Protection rests on one land run, and the water run contradicts it. 8. Mark superseded design decisions as such: the x3 pack bonus ('Decided yes' vs SW7 remove), the sneak bonus (vs SW2 retire), 'gate seasons with NO_<season>' (vs v7.0), the 5x gate, v1 rules, v2/v2.1/third-round Q&A and the mechanistic version all go to a design-history appendix. The lake-apex gap reopens now that fishers are off. 9. Fix the numeric slips: DOM2's 37/88 attacks include the dogs' 29/38; S8's 'deaths per surface arrival' divides cavern-native deaths by surface arrivals; wolf kills do not rise monotonically with prey slowness (elephant 3 < buffalo 7); the realm counts sum to 382, not 308; the roster cell count (68,000 vs 133,280) and 8,190 vs 601 don't reconcile; the triage counts don't match T0-triage.tsv; FSH2 lost three grizzlies, not two; the Fisher p = 0.35 is for 3/28, not 2/16. 10. Restructure as summary (findings with n) -> methods (forts, ticks to days, placement and cell-order biases, vacuous runs) -> results by topic (merge first-day single runs with their replications) -> one recommendations table with evidence strength and current status -> pending decisions -> appendices (block index, glossary of block and guild codes, design history, tracker, data/versions). Write the body in the third person rather than 'your ruling'.
